newsitem.title: USA: Conrail, CSX, Norfolk Southern meeting ends.
newsitem.headline: Conrail, CSX, Norfolk Southern meeting ends.

text.p: Conrail Inc, CSX Corp and Norfolk Southern Corp said they have concluded their meeting, but declined to comment on the session that was considered key to the future of the proposed Conrail-CSX merger.

"Conrail, CSX and Norfolk Southern have concluded their meeting and have agreed that no further details on this meeting or timing of future meetings will be announced," the companies said in a joint statement.

The meeting between chief executives David LeVan of Conrail, John Snow of CSX and David Goode of Norfolk Southern, was held in an attempt to resolve a stalemate in the three-month takeover battle for Philadelphia-based Conrail.

Conrail has repeatedly said it is committed to its proposed $9.6 billion merger with CSX despite a rival $10.3 billion bid from Norfolk Southern. Conrail shareholders earlier this month defeated a key provision that would have permitted the planned merger to move forward.

Norfolk Southern, which is in the process of buying 9.9 percent of Conrail's stock, has said it would not accept any type of resolution to the stalemate unless it valued Conrail at Norfolk Southern's bid of $115 per share.
The meeting reportedly took place in Washington, where all three executives were slated to attend the quarterly conference of the American Association of Railroads.
